traceability.notes:
All acceptance criteria and listed requirements for Story 001.0-DEV-PLUGIN-SETUP are fully implemented and verified:
- Core Functionality: The plugin exports a standard ESLint plugin object (`rules`, `configs`, `meta`, `maintenance`), dynamically loads rule modules, and is verified by `tests/plugin-setup.test.ts` and `tests/plugin-default-export-and-configs.test.ts`, which pass in the Jest run. - Quality Standards: `src/index.ts` follows ESLint plugin conventions, exposes `meta` derived from package.json with `name`, `version`, and `namespace`, and matches the documented patterns in `docs/eslint-plugin-development-guide.md`. - Integration (ESLint v9 flat config): The `configs.recommended` and `configs.strict` presets are implemented as flat-config fragments and tested via `tests/config/flat-config-presets-integration.test.ts`, which confirms they enable `traceability/require-story-annotation` when combined with a base config. README and the ESLint 9 setup guide show correct usage. - User Experience: README and `user-docs/eslint-9-setup-guide.md` provide clear installation instructions, version constraints, and concrete flat-config examples for JS, TS, and mixed projects, aligned with the actual plugin API. - Error Handling: `src/index.ts` wraps dynamic rule loading in try/catch, logs detailed errors, and installs a placeholder rule that reports an ESLint error instead of failing plugin load. `tests/plugin-setup-error.test.ts` validates this behavior, and `tests/cli-error-handling.test.ts` verifies the CLI exits non-zero and reports a missing-annotation message when configured with the plugin, both passing in the test run. - Documentation: Plugin structure, configs, and development guidance are documented in `docs/eslint-plugin-development-guide.md` and `docs/custom-rules-development-guide.md`, satisfying the documentation acceptance criterion.
Given the passing tests, inspected implementation, and up-to-date documentation, this story is fully satisfied.
